name: Monocytes (%)
rangeNote: A percentage depends on the total white cell count. The absolute monocyte count (cells per litre) is often more useful.
summary: Monocytes are white blood cells that clear away germs and damaged cells and help control inflammation. This value is their share of all white cells.

high.meaning: A higher share of monocytes is common while recovering from an infection and with long-lasting infections or inflammation. A share that stays raised for months is worth discussing with your doctor.
commonCauses: Inflammatory conditions, such as inflammatory bowel disease or rheumatic disease
Blood disorders such as chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia (rare)

low.meaning: A lower share often just means other white cells, usually neutrophils, have risen. On its own it rarely means much.
commonCauses: Other white cells raised, for example by a bacterial infection
Treatments that slow the bone marrow, such as chemotherapy

sources.title: Differential Diagnosis and Workup of Monocytosis: A Systematic Approach to a Common Hematologic Finding
